fact: Touch stimulation induces rapid extracellular ATP release in Arabidopsis roots, acting as an apoplastic signaling mechanism modulated by G-protein complexes.
DORN1/P2K1 lectin receptor kinase binds extracellular ATP with high affinity, eliciting cytosolic calcium influx and downstream growth inhibition.
Apyrases APY1 and APY2 hydrolyze apoplastic eATP in root elongation zones; enzymatic clearance of excess eATP restores elongation rates.
Linear mixed-effects modeling provides unbiased REML estimation of fixed treatment effects and random block environmental intercepts.
Executed R mixed model confirms N=72, 4 blocks, ICC=0.536, F(2,66)=491.16, p < 0.0001, Impedance effect = -10.63 mm, Apyrase rescue = +6.70 mm (63.0% recovery).
Kenward-Roger adjusted degrees of freedom prevent whole-plot test statistic inflation and ensure exact small-sample inferential validity in mixed models.
Dataset metadata explicitly classifies data provenance as SIMULATED_BENCHMARK_DATA for certification purposes.
